Simultaneously, the reuse of green materials provides several advantages, including maintaining ecological balance, reducing waste, conserving resources, saving energy, and achieving cost efficiency. Recognizing these advantages, researchers are focusing on predicting household garbage to facilitate the proper reuse of green materials. This paper examines various techniques for forecasting household garbage yields using machine learning models. The study selects monthly yield data from household waste as the time series and extracts seasonal information. The results of the prediction are compared with the additive seasonal ARIMA (SARIMA) model, autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), and simple exponential smoothing(SES). SARIMA models offer distinct approaches that automatically detect seasonality and trends. Performance evaluation of the prediction utilizes generic metrics such as the normalized form of mean square error (NMSE), normalized form of mean absolute error (NMAE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). The findings indicate that the prediction accuracy of the ARIMA model with NMSE of 1.42, NMAE of 0.09, and MAPE of 0.08 surpasses that of the SARIMA model and SES model. The insights from this study are beneficial for planning waste classification strategies developed recently. Yield estimation can greatly benefit our metropolis by enhancing domestic waste reuse opportunities.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Liver Disease Patient Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Liver disease is a significant global health concern, necessitating the development of accurate and efficient diagnostic tools. This study presents a comparative analysis of various machine learning classifiers, including Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost, and Ensemble Models, for the classification of liver disease patients. The challenge of class imbalance in the dataset is addressed using Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), ensuring a more balanced and representative training process. Missing data is handled with the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) Imputer, while Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) is employed to select the most relevant features, optimizing the model’s performance. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of these approaches, with a detailed comparison of each classifier’s performance in terms of accuracy and F1-score. This study provides valuable insights into the strengths and limitations of different machine learning classifiers for liver disease classification, contributing to the advancement of predictive modeling in healthcare.

articleTitle: Speech Emotion Recognition for a Tribal Language using Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Emotion is the most powerful tool for communicating ideas and behaviours to another person. Speech-emotion recognition is essential for comprehending another person’s inner workings since human communication mostly depends on the capacity to read one another’s emotions. The suggested intelligent system may perform better by classifying emotions by integrating machine learning classifiers with time and frequency-based acoustic features. The KUI is a tribal dataset with limited resources used in this study. Speech may be used to extract emotion through its temporal and spectral properties. Multi-layer perceptron (MLP), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Decision Tree (DT) classifiers are used to classify emotions from the supplied wave signal. These models have been trained to recognize theseସଡାଙଗ (Angry), ରେହା (Happy), ଆଜ (Fear), ବକାଲ (Sad), ବଜାର (Disgust), ଡେକ (Surprise)). The authors measured Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-Score to determine which model is optimal for the research. Among the four models, the SVM model has the highest accuracy of 94% and has the best precision rate, recall rate, and F1-Score forଆଜ(Fear) emotion.

articleTitle: Plant Leaf Diseases: Feature Extraction and Identification Using Convolutional Neural Networks and GLCM features
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: The economics of a nation is greatly impacted by agricultural production, and identifying diseases of plant leaves is essential to preserving yield quantity and quality. This study demonstrates a novel deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN) technique for detecting plant leaf disease. Plant leaf photos are first preprocessed using AMA (Adaptive Mean Adjustment) method to improve them and used a 2D Adaptive Anisotropic Diffusion Filter (hereafter 2D AADF) to remove noise. An improved method of segmentation is to use Adaptive Otsu (AO) thresholding along with Enhanced Fast Fuzzy C Means Clustering (hereafter EFFCMC). After extracting Grey Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) features from segmented pictures, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is used to reduce the dimensionality. In experiments, the new DCNN architecture-which consists of two fully linked layers, a SoftMax layer, and four convolutional layers-achieves better classification results.

articleTitle: Advanced Deep Learning Approaches for Content-Based Image Retrieval System in Skin Cancer Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to develop and assess the performance of a deep learning model-based content skin cancer detection image retrieval system. In this regard, CNN, VGGNet, ResNet, DenseNet, InceptionNet, and MobileNet were tested on recall, accuracy, mean average precision, F1, and precision metrics. VGGNet performed best among them, with an accuracy of 92.3%, outperforming all other models in precision, F1-score, and recall. CNN also gave the best performance with 91.5% accuracy. The CBIR system retrieved relevant images for the given lesions, especially melanoma lesions, which were relevant and high in precision within the top 5 retrieved images. These results also confirm the efficiency of CNN and VGGNet in enhancing accuracy during the retrieval of skin cancer diagnosis images.

articleTitle: Autonomous Vehicle Utilizing Deep Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: In today’s fast-paced world, individuals are constantly seeking ways to optimize their time and safety, especially during commutes and travel. Time management, traffic congestion, and safety are critical aspects of driving that have driven researchers to develop autonomous vehicles. A critical challenge in developing autonomous vehicles is achieving reliable lateral motion control. This paper addresses this issue by leveraging the deep learning techniques, and specifically explores the benefits of the NVIDIA Udacity car simulator. Our approach involves training a convolutional neural network (CNN) model to simulate the human driving behavior by utilizing a dataset of images and corresponding steering angles recorded during manual driving sessions in the simulator. It also emphasizes the importance of preprocessing the visual data to enhance the accuracy of the steering predictions. Our model is capable of managing complex driving scenarios within a simulated environment without the risks associated with real-world testing. A Mean Squared Error of 0.0123422 and an R-squared value of 0.8587687 suggest that our model is highly effective at navigating the car across different unfamiliar tracks.

articleTitle: Enhancing PCOS Prediction Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a prevalent endocrine disorder among women of reproductive age, requiring timely diagnosis and intervention to manage associated health risks. This research explores the application of various machine learning (ML) techniques for detecting PCOS, providing a comparative analysis of nine advanced methodologies: Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), Isolation Forest, Factorization Machines (FM), Multivariate Gaussian Process (MGP), Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF), Gaussian Processes (GP), Deep Belief Networks (DBN), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). The integration of Explainable AI techniques enhances the interpretability of these models, offering greater transparency in the decision-making process. The study leverages a dataset containing PCOS-related data to validate the proposed approach, evaluating the strengths and limitations of each ML model in terms of accuracy, interpretability, and diagnostic capability. This research aims to bridge the gap between advanced computational techniques and clinical applications, contributing to the growing field of ML-driven healthcare diagnostics. The findings highlight the potential of combining diverse machine learning frameworks to improve early detection and personalized treatment strategies for PCOS, ultimately improving patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Integrated System Optimization for Enhanced Performance of a Physical Model: A MATLAB and Python Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: This paper focuses on the development and optimization of a temperature control system utilizing a Proportional Integral-Derivative (PID) controller, with integration of MATLAB and Python. The work presented in this paper is structured around three key stages. The first stage involves the implementation of PID controllers using MATLAB’s toolbox tuning capabilities to establish a robust foundation for the temperature control system. In the second stage, Fuzzy Inference Systems (FIS) are employed to fine-tune the PID parame-ters-proportional ($K_{p}$), integral ($K_{i}$), and derivative ($K_{d}$)-to provide adaptability to varying system conditions, with the goal of enhancing system responsiveness and stability. The third and final stage introduces an innovative approach by integrating Python code into MATLAB Simulink for the design of a Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC). Initially, the MATLAB PID Tuner App is used to automatically tune the PID parameters, establishing a basic system framework. In the second stage, the FLC is incorporated with the PID controller to improve key performance metrics such as overshoot, settling time, and rise time. The third stage further refines this by replacing the FLC with a MATLAB Function Block in Simulink, allowing for seamless integration of Python scripts. This integration enables the application of advanced algorithms and computations, thereby expanding the control system’s capabilities and facilitating the use of more sophisticated control strategies and analysis techniques.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approach for Diabetes Prediction With a Tkinter–Based User Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Diabetes prediction is a critical task in healthcare that can significantly benefit from advancements in machine learning and deep learning technologies. This paper presents a hybrid approach combining deep learning and traditional machine learning models for diabetes prediction. The proposed system integrates a Tkinter-based Graphical User Interface (GUI) to make it easier for users to interact and make predictions. In our discussion, we will cover the design and implementation of the system, and evaluate the performance of different models using precision, F1 score, recall, and, accuracy to provide insights into their effectiveness. Results demonstrate the efficacy of the hybrid approach, with a focus on model accuracy and user experience.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Integration as virtual inertia for frequency control in two-area hybrid microgrid system
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: This article discusses the development and analysis of a two-area load frequency control (LFC) hybrid microgrid system that integrates both renewable and conventional energy sources. In each area, renewable energy sources are integrated alongside conventional generators to enhance system sustainability and reliability. A proposed 2-degree of freedom tilt integral derivative fuzzy (2-DOF TIDF FUZZY) controller is designed and implemented to investigate its effectiveness in minimizing the fluctuations in tie-line power and frequency under varying load conditions. Additionally, an Electric Vehicle (EV) is employed as virtual inertia to dampen oscillations in frequency deviations caused by random load changes, thereby improving system stability. Simulation results show that the proposed control strategy excels in maintaining frequency stability and minimizing tie-line power deviations, providing a strong solution for future microgrid applications.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Mobility: A comprehensive Review of Vehicular Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Vehicular communication networks (VCNs) are often referred to V2X communication and are crucial for addressing traffic related issues, interoperability issues and reliability issues such as high speed, connectivity in the near future as the automotive industry experiences a revolutionary transition towards connected and autonomous vehicles. This extensive overview delves into the latest developments, difficulties, and possible uses in the field of VCNs. In addition, the study looks into how VCNs are being integrated with cutting-edge technologies like ML and AI to provide improved traffic management, predictive maintenance, and intelligent decision-making processes.

articleTitle: A Novel RCNN-CNN Hybrid Framework for Emotion Recognition in Facial Expressions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: In several domains like affective computing, neurology, and human-computer interfaces, facial emotion detection plays a significant role. This research explores an innovative approach of employing CNNs and RCNNs conjointly for facial emotion recognition. The combined model increases both the accuracy and efficiency in the identification and categorization of specific emotions from facial expressions by using the advantages of RCNN in region assignment and CNN in feature extraction. Impressive results were obtained from the evaluation of the integrated RCNN-CNN model: The following results were achieved: 98.7% accuracy, 98.5% precision, 98.9% recall, and 98.7% F1-Score. This empirical shows how good is the recommended method at pinpointing the emotions exactly. Further, the research focuses on how the technique can help in fields such as human-computer interaction, emotional computing, and psychology education. Toward this goal, improvements will be made in the model’s ability to go beyond basic interactions and explore its scalability and applicability in real-world scenarios. In a nutshell, this study signifies progress in the area of facial emotion identification as well as creates the potential for human-machine interactions to be more empathetic and more compassionate.

articleTitle: A Systematic Analysis of Multi-Property Prediction Using Deep Learning In The Field Of Drug Development
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: In the rapidly changing field of pharmaceutical development, it is crucial to speed up clinical trials in order to introduce effective drugs in a timely manner. Conventional methods of forecasting molecular characteristics are often slow and time consuming, causing difficulties in the drug discovery process. However, Advancements in deep learning have streamlined pharmaceutical testing, enabling precise prediction of key drug properties like solubility, toxicity, reactivity, and bioactivity before synthesis. By employing different Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (SMILES) representations and training them with various deep learning algorithms like Graph Neural Networks (GNN) and Graph Convolution Networks (GCN). In this, a comparative study done on various technologies used in predicting molecular properties that helps to develop faster clinical trials in pharmaceutical industry. By identifying the limitations in the existing technologies, proposed an improved GCN which helps in better estimation of molecular properties.

articleTitle: Architectural Model of Deep Convolution Neural Network Approach for Brain Tumor Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is most commonly used technique to detect a tumor by physicians in medical science. The MRI images are three-dimensional images with the number of slices that are analyzed to identify the defective cells in the naked eye that leads to a time-consuming process. Machine Learning (ML) techniques are investigated as a solution to improve tumor identification in a better way. Early and accurate detection is crucial for effective treatment planning and improving patient outcomes. Traditionally, brain tumor diagnosis relies on manual analysis of MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) scans by radiologists, which can be time-consuming and prone to human error. The advent of deep learning, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), has opened new avenues for automating and improving the accuracy of brain tumor prediction. In this paper, we study the Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) model which is popular in image analysis. Similar way, we develop a CNN model to process and classify the MRI images to detect the type of brain tumor. We examine the model’s performance by using 5712 MRI images from a standard dataset available in the public domain. The aim of the work is to classify the tumor in four classes like: Glioma, Meningioma, Pituitary and No Tumour using the proposed CNN model. Our model follows data preprocessing, image encoding, filtering and classification. The proposed model scores 78% accuracy as its performance in the dataset which needs more investigations and comparison with other techniques in further study.

articleTitle: Motor Imagery Classification in EEG signals using Hybrid CNN-ISqueeze net
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Motor imagery (MI) electroencephalography (MI-EEG) data are widely used in BCI systems to determine participant intention. MI classification is challenging because of several reasons, such as poor signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) and lack of excellent data. The operation of BCI devices requires an understanding of MI-EEG signals. Recent years have seen the effective use of deep learning (DL) techniques in recognizing patterns and other domains. Conversely, there aren’t many efficient DL algorithms that have been used with BCI systems. This research work presents a novel MIC scheme using the hybrid classifier. At first, the EEG signals are preprocessed by applying the band pass filtering (BPF) method. Then, features including Stockwell transform (ST), correntropy and Common Spatial Pattern (CSP) features are extracted. For MIC, a hybrid classification method that combines CNN and Improved squeeze net (ISQN) is employed in this work.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Neurodevelopmental Disorders: Quantifying Autism Behavioral Markers with Computer Vision and Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is traditionally diagnosed through clinical observation and standardized tests, processes that are time-consuming and require expert intervention. Early detection is crucial for effective intervention, yet current methods often delay diagnosis, particularly in resource-limited settings. This study presents a scalable, non-invasive method for early autism detection using standard webcam technology to measure biomarkers associated with ASD. The system captures and analyzes eye-tracking data, head movements, and behavioral responses during a controlled 4 -minute video presentation. Data is processed through a series of carefully selected machine learning models, with the most advanced model—utilizing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with ResNet layers—achieving an 91% accuracy rate. Our pilot study, involving 147 children, resulted in the creation of a proprietary dataset, supporting the robustness of this method.

articleTitle: Exploring the Link between Corporate Sustainability and Organizational Performance in Indian Public Companies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: The purpose of the study was to investigate the relationship between organisational success and corporate sustainability in publicly traded Indian enterprises. Variables for corporate sustainability and non-financial organisational performance were created by academics using text analysis of 281 sustainability reports from a sample of 100 companies between 2016 and 2019. Indices of financial success were developed using accepted research as a basis. Companies were divided into groups based on the level of corporate sustainability (DCS) in order to examine the connections between organisational success and corporate sustainability. The non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test revealed a statistically significant variation in these groups’ medians. To show these associations, boxplot graphs were used. The results showed a favourable correlation between an organization’s organisational performance-both non-financial and financial-and its DCS. The ROE (Return on Equity) and ROA (Return on Assets) variables, however, did not show any discernible changes. This study adds to the body of knowledge on performance assessments by concentrating on factors other than only the financial and economic. It also emphasises how publicly traded Indian corporations can use the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) as a gauge of corporate sustainability.

articleTitle: Predicting Marketing Campaign Effectiveness through Consumer Personality Analysis using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Understanding customer behavior and personality is essential for marketing campaign. It might help huge corporations comprehend their purchasing behavior. Companies directed by their marketers can conduct product marketing activities that are specific to the customer’s personality attributes. This study examines the use of various classification models to evaluate client personality attributes and predict marketing campaign performance by customer response after marketing campaign. Response of the customer was the target feature and it is a binary classification. Feature engineering has also been applied for optimal feature selection. Several machine learning classifier algorithms, including Gradient Boosting (GB), Ada Boost (AB), Cat Boost (CB), Voting Classifier (VC), Stacking Classifier (SC), K Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), and Logistic Regression (LR) were implemented after the dataset had been preprocessed and normalized. Several matrices were employed for comparing the performance of these models. The Stacking Classifier emerged to be the best performing model with accuracy of 0.8988.

articleTitle: Employing YOLO model for traffic monitoring on roadways
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: With the advent of advanced computer vision techniques and the support of Deep learning models, it has become very feasible to do traffic analysis. This study explores the creation of analytical and computer vision algorithms for traffic analysis which can precisely detect, track, count and analyze traffic situations. An efficient traffic analysis would ensure safety and proper urban planning. This paper proposes a deep learning based intelligent system which would perform automatic vehicle detection, tracking and counting of three different types of vehicles namely, car, bus and truck. One of the prominent deep learning models - YOLO was selected and employed for this purpose. Competitive analysis of different YOLO models is performed for various parameters, where YOLOv8 emerges out to be the winner, which gives an accuracy more than of $\mathbf{9 7 \%}$ at a decent processing time.

articleTitle: Evaluating Object Detection Approaches for Fruit Detection in Precision Agriculture: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Agricultural automation has become increasingly vital in addressing the growing demand for food and the need for efficient farming practices. Fruit harvesting is crucial in agriculture due to its labor intensity and the challenges of timely, accurate picking under occlusions and varying illumination. Various methods have been developed for accurate fruit detection, but traditional techniques often struggle with occlusions by branches or leaves, as well as challenges posed by climate and fruit maturity. This study reviews existing literature, compares various fruit detection approaches and discusses their strengths and weaknesses. Building on the work of various authors, this paper aims to offer a thorough understanding of the current state of fruit detection technologies in agricultural automation. Additionally, the survey addresses the objective of the proposed work, which is to identify the most promising techniques for improving fruit detection accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: NeuroForest: Combining CNN and Random Forest for Superior Lung Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Using a hybrid model combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Random Forest classifiers, using histopathology images, this study offers a fresh technique for lung cancer detection. Using a collection of 4,257 labelled lung tissue pictures, the work painstakingly preprocessed to guarantee uniformity and quality. Extensive features from the photos were extracted using the CNN, which had three convolutional layers followed by max-pooling and another set of three convolutional layers. Then, utilising 15 decision trees in a Random Forest, these characteristics were categorised. The accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, as well as specificity showed the model’s performance is $\mathbf{76.}\mathbf{69\%}$ all-around. In specific, the dimension changes in many forms of lung cancer cells particularly and the results indicated the strong detecting capability of the method. As for the evaluation of the model, it was observed the need to improve, with important results in reduce false positives and false negatives, identified in confusion matrix. High performance for automated lung cancer diagnosis when it comes to this hybrid paradigm: CNN’s feature extraction option and Random Forest’s classification option. Summarising the promotion of deep learning in enhancing the accuracy of cancer diagnosis, the paper concludes with better improvement and future research direction.

articleTitle: AI Enabled Digital Twin Models to Enhance Security in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: As smart cities continue to expand, the security of interconnected systems, such as smart grids, water distribution, and waste management, is paramount. Traditional security measures often lack the predictive capabilities needed to identify and counter cyber threats effectively, posing risks to these critical infrastructures. This research investigates the use of AIenabled digital twin models to strengthen security in smart city environmental management systems. Utilizing Autodesk Tandem as the digital twin platform, we simulate these subsystems and integrate a machine learning (ML) model to monitor network fluctuations, simulate cyber-attacks, and evaluate response strategies. Specifically, a Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) model, trained on the CICIDS2017 dataset, is applied to detect threats in real time. By observing subsystem behavior under attack conditions, we identify vulnerabilities and develop enhanced preventive measures. This approach seeks to create a robust security framework capable of predicting, detecting, and mitigating cyber threats in smart city infrastructures.

articleTitle: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence for Enhancing Performance and Preventing Injuries in Sports Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: The sports sector could see a revolution in player performance enhancement and injury prevention, especially with recent developments in artificial intelligence (AI). In order to identify areas for improvement and potential injury risks, this proposed work aims to utilize the potential of AI techniques, such as XGBoost, to evaluate extensive player data, including movement patterns, biomechanics, and physical condition. This strategy is unusual because it combines real-time feedback systems with AI-powered predictive modeling to offer athletes and coaches individualized training advice and early warnings about potential injury risks. Cleaning and normalization were done during the preparation phase to make sure the data was suitable for analysis. Utilizing XGBoost for feature extraction allowed for the identification of critical factors affecting efficiency and injury risk. In sports analytics, the suggested XGBoost-AI system was compared to other AI-based techniques for improving performance and avoiding injuries. The study’s findings show that the XGBoost classifier significantly improves performance accuracy, which may reach 96%. This is in contrast to conventional approaches that depend on subjective evaluations and human data analysis, which can result in errors and inefficiencies. Python is used to implement the suggested work. AI-driven sports analytics platform can improve game strategy, fan engagement, and data-driven decision-making for sports organizations, enhancing competitiveness and sustainability in the sports industry.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of digital mammograms using computer-assisted system: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: In recent decades, breast cancer has been consid ered the leading cause of death in Women. Therefore, raising awareness about early detection and diagnosis of breast cancer is extremely important to prevent severity of breast cancer and to improve the quality of life of patients. Digital mammography is widely recognized as an efficient and accurate tool for the early and accurate detection of breast abnormalities. The healthcare imaging sector continues to actively design and develop a reliable, error-free computer-aided diagnostic (CAD) system for automated diagnosis of digital mammograms for the past few decades. Traditional approaches to the clinical examination of mammogram images often require significant labor costs and are highly dependent on clinical expertise, leading to inherent variability. In contrast, Artificial Intelligence (AI), including Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques, has emerged as a valuable technology in breast cancer diagnosis using mammography images to reduce diagnostic error rates and improve accuracy. Taking this fact into account, this paper reviews the current state of research on digital mammogram detection and classification using ML and DL techniques. It emphasizes explicitly recent advancements in ML and DL techniques for analyzing digital mammography images and offers perspectives on future developments.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Crime Types and Occurrences Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: This paper review focuses on the potential of applying machine learning algorithms such as K-Nearest Neighbours, Naïve Bayes, Random Forest, and Artificial Neural Network to analyze crime prediction by type and occurrence at specific locations and times and regarding historical data of similar scenarios. From these studies, it is possible to conclude that applying these predictive models can be beneficial when sharing knowledge with law enforcement agencies, particularly regarding optimized resource allocation and strategic security plans. Further research may focus on improving the prediction of new types of threats through stronger ensemble methods, transfer learning between cities, and real-time processing to adapt to changes in crime characteristics. It ultimately helps to reduce the risk to residents and prevent more crime incidents.

articleTitle: An Efficient Machine Learning Based Models for Anomaly Detection in Network Traffic
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Currently, anomaly detection in the network is a major concern of the day’s network clients in this age of advancement in technology. Network security has become paramount due to the increased number and volume of sophisticated computer crimes. There are many threats to the networks, and the most common are network anomalies that can result in system failures and inhibit the proper functioning of the networks. Though their efficacy in identifying network anomalies has been established, algorithms using Machine Learning and Deep Learning are still relatively unknown. This work’s objective is to thoroughly examine many methods for detecting network anomalies in Machine Learning. Using Machine Learning techniques on the NSL-KDD dataset-used for outlier identification-this study aims to enhance network intrusion detection. Comprehensive data preprocessing was undertaken to prepare the dataset for robust analysis. The study focused on multi-class and binary classification tasks, using Voting Classifier ensembles combining multi-layer perceptron with random forest and logistic regression with decision trees. The Voting Classifier models provided very high accuracy, whereas the multi-class model was found to have an accuracy of $\mathbf{99.} \mathbf{93 \%}$, while the binary-class model had an accuracy of 99. $\mathbf{82 \%}$, this makes the system very accurate, relying on the ensemble techniques to enhance the reliability and precision of an intrusion detection system.

articleTitle: Flood Forecasting with Classical and Quantum Machine Learning Models: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Flood forecasting is one of the most disastrous natural phenomena; however, its prediction with sufficient accuracy can help to at least reduce the damage caused by this potentially disastrous event. Additionally, in this paper, a comparison of classical and quantum models for machine learning in flood forecasting is made. Traditional machine learning means have found wide use in view of this, particularly when there exist historical data and a number of environmental parameters. But with the strength that quantum computing holds, quantum machine learning models are poised for even better predictive accuracy and efficiency for the future, as they have the capability to process loads of data all at once. In this text, we implement both the classical models, such as the Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forests, alongside quantum machine learning models. We compare on prediction accuracy, computational efficiency, and scalability. The results will point out the strengths and limitations of each approach, from which it will be possible to derive how quantum machine learning can complement or surpass the performances of classical methods for the improved reliability and timeliness of predictions in flood forecasting.

articleTitle: Milk Grade-Guard: Enhancing Food Safety Through ML
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: In the dairy industry, the safety of the milk is crucial. On the other hand, conventional ways of evaluating quality could have drawbacks. Milk Grade-Guard is a cuttingedge strategy that uses machine learning (ML) to improve food safety. The potential of machine learning techniques to evaluate a large data set of milk quality along the supply chain is examined in this paper. Beyond conventional techniques, ML can spot minor signs of tainted milk that might go unnoticed otherwise. This feature can greatly enhance the evaluation of milk quality and allow for the early identification of any contamination or spoiling. Milk Grade-Guard provides a multifaceted strategy to improve food safety. The solution can eliminate human error, save costs related to manual testing, and streamline operations by automating quality assessments using machine learning. More significantly, less product waste is produced and dangerous milk is kept from reaching customers thanks to early problem detection enabled by ML-powered prediction. In order to confirm Milk Grade-Guard’s function in strengthening food safety protocols within the dairy industry, more investigation and development are necessary.

articleTitle: Innovative Approach for Early Detection and Risk Assessment of Lung Cancer Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Lung cancer remains an ongoing global health challenge, necessitating the development of innovative methods for early detection and risk assessment. This study presents a comprehensive approach for predicting lung cancer by utilizing a carefully curate dataset consisting of 1000 individuals from Kaggle dataset. The cutting-edge machine learning models, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), Naive Bayes Multinomial (NBM), Meta Bagging, PART and Random Forest (RF are used to enhance the accuracy of our predictions. The dataset we’ve compiled includes a wide array of patient characteristics, encompassing demographics, lifestyle factors, medical history, and health data gathered through IoT devices. By harnessing the capabilities of IoT technology, it is possible to enable real-time and continuous health monitoring, facilitating a dynamic assessment of lung cancer risk. The finding of this study reveal that the PART model achieves an impressive accuracy of 95%, surpassing other models like NBM (67%), RF (93%), SVM (92%), and Bagging (86%). This innovative approach shows promise in the early detection of lung cancer and the provision of personalized risk assessments, potentially leading to improved patient outcomes and reduced healthcare burdens.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Classification using VGG19 Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Accurate and timely diagnosis of brain tumors is very crucial for appropriate treatment planning and proper management of the patient. In the past years, deep learning has influenced medical image analysis, mainly in relation to classifying tumors using medical imaging techniques. The article proposed a framework for classifying brain tumors with the use of a deep learning model based on the VGG19 architecture with MRI images sourced from the comprehensive Kaggle dataset containing 7,023 annotated images. The proposed model utilizes the strengths of deep convolutional neural networks in automatically extracting relevant features from those complex MRI images to optimize the classification process. After an extensive process of preprocessing, augmentation, and a thorough training protocol, the VGG19 model was established, such that it achieved an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9. 1 7 \%}$ on the validation set. Such high accuracy underscores the efficacy of using deep learning approaches for medical imaging and, more importantly, serves as an injunction for further investigations into automated diagnostic systems that could be handy in supporting the clinician toward better patient outcomes and an enhancement in diagnostic workflows.

articleTitle: Software Fault Forecasting through Puffer-fish Optimization Algorithm-based Feature Selection Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Software Fault Forecasting (SFF) identifies faults earlier in the software advancement procedure. However, it is vital to address the issue of high dimensionality to achieve an effective fault forecasting model. Feature selection (FS) is an effective technique to identify the best features from a dataset. This study proposes an innovative FS approach, referred to as POAFS rooted on the Puffer-fish Optimization Algorithm (POA) to extract the best traits from a software dataset. POAFS draws inspiration from the puffer-fish’s defense strategy from the predator’s attack. The proposed POAFS approach was examined on five public NASA datasets using a four-supervised learning classifier, namely Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, K-nearest neighbour, and Decision Tree. The investigatory findings revealed that the prospective POAFS proposal substantially enhanced the veracity of the fault forecasting model besides achieving the superior features.

articleTitle: Modified Deep Neural Network Approach to Identify Heart Disease using IoMT: Artificial Neural Networks or Convolutional Neural Networks!
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Unconventional methods of predicting and treating heart disease (HD) are required because HD is still the top mortality on a global scale. This study delves into the potential of combining deep learning (DL) methods with IoMT devices to improve HD prediction and early diagnosis. Despite their usefulness, traditional risk assessment approaches can misrepresent the intricate relationship between cardiovascular risk factors. On the other hand, DL and ML algorithms can sift through mountains of data related to lifestyle, genetics, demographics, and clinical conditions to find complex relationships. To increase generalization performance across varied patient demographics and datasets, our study is focused on designing a novel DL architecture that is specialized for HD prediction. We optimize its design and hyperparameters. With feature engineering, when selecting features, we use linear discriminant analysis (LDA). In our work, two different DL techniques neural network and convolutional neural network (CNN) for HD identification are studied. We then evaluate the studied model’s efficacy with measures including recall, accuracy, precision, F1-score, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). By attaining 96% accuracy, 97% precision, 95% specificity, 97% F1-score, and 93% MCC on chosen features, the experimental findings show that a one-dimensional (1-D) CNN performs better than other models. Our suggested method, which combines DL and IoMT, offers a powerful answer to the problems of real-time health monitoring and HD risk assessment, which in turn improves early intervention and tailors treatment plans to each patient. The findings of this study highlight the promise of cutting-edge AI-driven approaches to revolutionizing cardiovascular healthcare.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Tax on Enterprises in Bengaluru: Insights from Poisson and Machine learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Small businesses in Bengaluru, particularly those categorized as Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), have encountered numerous challenges, especially amid the ongoing pandemic lockdowns. However, the initial turbulence experienced during the GST rollout appears to have subsided for many MSMEs in Bengaluru. This study aims to explore the perceptions and impacts of GST on local small businesses. Factors such as satisfaction and awareness regarding GST are also examined. A structured questionnaire survey was conducted to collect responses from MSME owners across Bengaluru. These responses underwent analysis using various statistical methods. Although the Poisson model struggles with more rounds, the Random Forest model provides improved fit and prediction accuracy, with an RMSE of 0.422. The findings suggest that perceptions of GST among Bengaluru’s MSMEs vary depending on the type of enterprise. Moreover, GST has gained widespread acceptance among MSMEs in the region, with many reporting positive impacts from its implementation. This study illuminates the nuances of GST’s effects on Bengaluru’s MSME sector, providing valuable insights for both theory and practice.

articleTitle: Smart Health Monitoring Wearable with Accessibility using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: In our day-to-day lives, monitoring health regularly is essential to ensure the body functions well under various conditions. This paper outlines the development of a smart health monitoring wearable device utilizing an Arduino Uno as the core processing unit. The device is designed to monitor health parameters continuously, transmitting data wirelessly for real-time analysis and feedback. Modern connectivity options enable data sharing with a centralized platform, allowing efficient health management and user interaction through mobile or web applications. This wearable aims to enhance healthcare by providing immediate health insights and alerting providers to potential health issues, embodying a proactive approach to health monitoring in everyday life.

articleTitle: A lightweight encrypted packet priority classification framework for Cognitive radio enabled Industrial IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Industrial IoT (IIoT) has been adopted due to its significant benefits in industrial operations. However, the rapid proliferation of IIoT devices raises concern about the spectrum shortage. Cognitive radio (CR) technology has been proposed as a potential solution to meet the increasing spectrum demand. CR enables IIoT devices to use the licensed spectrum bands opportunistically. Due this exponential growth of IIoT devices, it has become nearly impossible to accommodate all spectrum demands from IIoT devices. To optimize resource management, it is important to classify the packets into different classes to ensure that at least critical packets can be accommodated within the available spectrum. However, categorizing the encrypted packets based on their information priority is complex. To address this challenge, we introduce a lightweight Packet Prioritization Framework (PPF) for CR enabled IIoT (CR-IIoT) networks. The PPF uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract complex spatial features from encrypted packets. We acknowledge that packets from the same IIOT device may have varying priorities depending on the sensed data. The model’s effectiveness is verified using the K-fold cross-validation technique. To ensure the model deployable on IIoT devices, we applied model compression techniques to make PPF lightweight. We created a custom dataset in a simulated IIoT network to evaluate the performance of PPF. Further, we conducted an exhaustive simulation to compare PPF with existing models to validate the accuracy, efficiency, and resource utilization of our model.

articleTitle: Enhancing Customer Churn Prediction in Telecommunication with CNN-Gradient Boosting Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: The telecommunications industry faces a constant challenge in retaining customers amidst fierce competition, making accurate churn prediction a critical aspect of business strategy. In this paper, we propose a novel hybrid model, implemented in Python, that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Gradient Boosting Machines (GBMs) to enhance customer churn prediction accuracy. Leveraging a comprehensive dataset encompassing demographic details, service usage, payment information, and customer support interactions, our model extracts intricate patterns from the data using CNNs and integrates them with traditional features for robust prediction. Through extensive experimentation and evaluation, we demonstrate that our proposed CNN-GBM model achieves an outstanding accuracy of 99%, surpassing other existing approaches by $\mathbf{2.6 \%}$. The model’s performance is evaluated using standard metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-Score, showcasing its superiority over traditional methods like Random Forest and Support Vector Machine. The CNN-GBM model’s remarkable accuracy and superior performance highlight its efficacy in accurately identifying churned customers while minimizing false positives, thus providing a valuable tool for telecom companies to implement targeted retention strategies. Moreover, our methodology offers scalability and generalizability, making it applicable across industries facing similar churn challenges. Overall, our proposed hybrid CNNGBM model presents a significant advancement in customer churn prediction, offering telecom companies a reliable solution to improve customer retention and competitiveness in the market.

articleTitle: High-Precision Fracture Identification: The Role of Convolutional Neural Networks in Orthopedics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: The research work is related to diagnosing a bone fracture using CNN on X-ray images. The collection is done by combining multi-region X-ray images and classifying them into two classes: bone fractured and non-fractured. This work illustrates a more precise classifying automated fracture detection, which is one of the critical needs in diagnoses of medicine. For effective treatment, early and precise identification of bone fractures is necessary by means of a diagnostic. The code implemented a CNN architecture using PyTorch and displayed the performance of the model on both the training and development sets. The result at the end of 30 epochs shows a development accuracy of $95.01 \%$ with a corresponding loss of 0.18, hence the model is very robust in classifying bone fractures in that regard. Tracking different performance metrics, such as accuracy and loss during epochs, prevents overfitting of the model. Concretely, it can enhance the clinical workflow by excluding most of the errors typical for manual diagnostics and hasten the process of identifying fractures, which will lead to better patient outcomes. These results further the existing works in the field of artificial intelligence in Healthcare and present a dependable solution to bone fracture detection that can be deployed in real-world clinical settings. Further work could be done in the direction of enlargement of this data set by increasing classes or other types of fractures and also optimizing the model to find out how the model can serve best in a clinical setting.

articleTitle: Binary Classification of Bone Fractures using Transfer Learning: A Comprehensive Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: In medical imaging, timely and accurate diagnosis of bone fractures is essential. This work offers a thorough approach to binary classification using VGG16 and ResNet architectures in Transfer Learning on X-ray images. In order to maximize model performance, the methodology includes extensive preprocessing steps like data augmentation, resizing, and normalization. The process of extracting features involves honing in on pre-trained models to capture complex fracture patterns. To improve the extracted features, Principal Component Analysis is used, which reduces dimensionality without sacrificing important information. The feature set is then processed by a machine learning classification algorithm, like Random Forest or Support Vector Machines, to enable accurate fracture detection. The efficacy of the suggested method is demonstrated by experimental validation carried out on various X-ray datasets, providing a comprehensive solution for accurate and efficient bone fracture diagnosis in medical imaging.

articleTitle: A Study on Object Detection using Faster R-CNN, Retina net, RPN_R_50_FPN, RPN_R_50_C4
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: The computer vision concept that involves the detection and characterization of objects in images is known as object detection. This research mainly performs this function using four popular models faster R-CNN, RetinaNet, RPN_R_50_FPN, and RPN_R_50_C4 across multiple datasets namely udacity self-driving car dataset, tomatOD dataset, and chess piece detection dataset. Faster R-CNN is famous for its outstanding accuracy although RetinaNet employs a unique focal loss function to balance between speed and accuracy. The purpose of the models RPN_R_50_FPN and RPN_R_50_C4 is to generate region proposals with high quality using different stages in the ResNet-50 backbone. For normalization techniques, the datasets are preprocessed in this research. Instead of training the models from scratch, transfer learning is used whereby starting with weights that were pre-trained on the COCO dataset and after that fine-tuning the required datasets. Accuracy was quantified by evaluating two efficiency measures which are minimum loss and total training duration. Across the different datasets, various performances were demonstrated by different models.

articleTitle: Innovative CNN Approaches for Brain Tumor Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Model Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: This research presents a comparative analysis of three state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks (CNNs)—InceptionV3, ResNet50, and VGG19—for classifying brain tumors from MRI images. Utilizing a diverse dataset divided into four categories (glioma, meningioma, notumor, and pituitary), the study evaluates model performance based on precision, recall, F1-score, and overall accuracy. VGG19 emerged as the best performer, achieving an impressive accuracy of $\mathbf{9 6\%}$, excelling in the precise identification of glioma and notumor cases with minimal misclassification. ResNet50 also performed well with 96% accuracy, showing balanced results across most categories but slightly underperforming in meningioma classification. InceptionV3, with a lower accuracy of 93%, struggled with meningioma detection. These findings highlight the growing potential of deep learning in medical diagnostics, positioning VGG19 as the most reliable model for brain tumor classification. In subsequent study, these models can be improved by using hybrid architectures and datasets that are more diverse to achieve better clinical outcomes in the real world.

articleTitle: Driver Facial Emotions and Drowsiness Detection for Enhanced Advanced Driver Assistance Systems(ADAS): Safety Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: The proposed approach seeks to recognize real-time emotions from human facial expressions. Facial emotions are the most essential visual indicators for identifying a driver’s emotional state and weariness. The framework work is developed to allow the computer to automatically extract the facial identification of human emotions using a deep face library and the amount of fatigue of eyes calculating eye-aspect-ratio (EAR) with Open CV2. From the results of our study, the model shows that if eyelids remain closed for longer than projected, this is a sign of weariness or drowsiness. A warning signal is provided to the driver if the system finds symptoms of sleepiness straight ahead concerning the driver’s safety on the road. The project proposes to construct a non-intrusive driver warning system as part of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) to increase the safety of all road users while driving.

articleTitle: Facial Emotion Recognition Through Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: With the assistance of artificial intelligence (AI), this study endeavoured to investigate emotion recognition. The exploration revolved around the detection and comprehension of human emotions; a task historically acknowledged as challenging. However, AI demonstrated the potential to usher in a paradigm shift within this industry. Facial expressions were subject to analysis through AI-based emotion detection systems, enabling a deeper understanding and identification of human emotions. Accuracy in recognition of emotion was achieved by using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in the image analysis component of facial expressions, thereby playing a crucial role. The implications of this research resonated across diverse domains, including sentiment analysis, emotion-aware systems, and educational technology, highlighting the importance of emotions in decision making and social interactions. To grasp the foundational principles of emotion recognition, the paper meticulously laid the groundwork, establishing a fundamental understanding of emotions. The discussion then delved into the analysis of facial expressions, which served as abundant resources for emotion recognition. For facial expressions, CNNs were employed to extract and analyse features, enhancing the precision of emotion detection. This study functioned as a primer for those intrigued by the captivating realm of AI-based emotion detection. It not only illuminated the foundational concepts within the field but also underscored its transformative potential in reshaping human-computer interactions and emotion detection technology, marking significant progress and laying the groundwork for a future in which AI, including CNNs, is ubiquitously employed.

articleTitle: Automated Cardiovascular Disease Detection from ECG Images Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Healthcare is one of the crucial parts of our lives, and currently heart attack is one of the major causes of death worldwide. It is essential to predict the cardiovascular disease at an early stage. The traditional approach of consulting the physician periodically is neglected due to ignorance in the society. Automatic heart disease prediction and detection system would save several lives. The four types of cardiac abnormalities are NP, AH, MI, and HMI. To predict the cardiac abnormalities this paper uses the CNN technique of Deep Learning. The heart disease dataset of ‘UCI Cleveland’ is used in our proposed model. The dropout technique is used in our proposed model to avoid overfitting. For performance measurement, Various performance parameters like precision, accuracy, F1 score, and Recall are considered. The accuracy of our CNN model is 94%, which shows the significant achievement for the prediction.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Survey on Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is a hot topic in the field of computer vision, natural language processing, and artificial intelligence. Nowadays, people share their reviews on products and services not only through text but also via audio, video, and images. The growing need for sentiment analysis across a wide range of channels of expression has made multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) a prominent area of study. This survey paper categorizes various MSA fusion architectures into ten distinct categories. Within each category, recent contributions are identified and discussed, highlighting their strengths and limitations. Finally, numerous applications, challenges, and future directions are explored.

articleTitle: Personified Emotion Detection from Speech using Supervised Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Speech-based emotion recognition in machine learning is an emerging topic. In our daily routine, whatever speech we communicate can be based on our mood or emotion that we intend to share. In our model we have tried to categorize different emotions into specific class such as happiness, sadness, anger, calm, surprise, disgust, neutral and fear. The model uses the feature extraction techniques to collect different features which will be helpful to classify into different classes. Machine learning algorithms such as SVM, KNN are applied to classify the emotions of a person in real-time. The proposed system has the potential to be used in various applications such as mental health monitoring, human-robot interaction and speech therapy. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves high accuracy in recognizing emotions from speech signals. The system’s performance can be further improved by using larger datasets, more advanced feature extraction methods, and deep learning algorithms. Overall, the proposed system has significant potential to recognise the human emotions for the well beings of an individual.

articleTitle: Consensus Clustering using Weights of Clusters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Consensus clustering is a technique that leverages an ensemble of clusterings produced by various algorithms to create a single, superior, and robust clustering. In this study, we propose the application of cluster weights to form the consensus, where the weights are derived from cluster-level information gathered from the diversity within the ensemble, as well as data distribution-level information from the internal quality of the clusterings. Our experimental results demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed weighting method compared to other recently proposed consensus clustering algorithms.

articleTitle: A Sentiment Analysis of Product Review Data Through Large Language Models (LLMs)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Opinion mining, which can be classified as process of extracting subjective information from text data, remains one of the most widely researched areas in NLP even today. Because of its ability to gauge thoughts and opinions of people it has garnered lot of interest from both scholars and practitioners. A Lot of advancement has been made in this area with the help of large language models (LLMs). This paper aims to compare the sentiment classification on Amazon product review dataset using the various types of LLMs, including BERT and TF-IDF models. Thus, the resultant dataset containing 59,794 total reviews was pre-processed and further split into the training and testing sets. When performing the Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) it was determined there were three sentiments; Positive, Negative and Neutral. The measurements, namely F1-score, recall, accuracy, and precision, were used to compare the performances of the developed models. Analysis showed that an accuracy of TF-IDF model was enhanced by 15.59% as compared to the BERT model that yielded an accuracy of only 78. 91%. This study further embraces the use of TF-IDF and LLM for sentiment analysis and highlights directions for future studies to improve the model reliability and efficiency by eradicating false prediction gaps and integrating other complicated approaches such as ensemble learning.

articleTitle: Cyber-Physical System for Real-Time Tracking and Monitoring of Rare Blood Donors in Emergencies by Enhancing Donor Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: In most of the places, in emergency basis arranging blood donors of rare blood group within short time period is a real challenge. there are several factor that may influence this challenge negatively. Such factors includes, unavailability of blood donors for rare type in emergencies, identification of potential donor, convincing potential donors to participate within short time period, and proper co-ordination of donor to reach the blood donation spot. In the current literature’s, all these factor are not integrated as a mechanism to facilitate easy, seamless and quick arrangement of rare blood donor in emergencies. This article proposed a novel Cyber-Physical System to accommodate all these factors to facilitate a easy, seamless and quick arrangement of rare blood in emergencies within a short time period.

articleTitle: The Contribution of Strategic Information Systems to Organizational Transformation and Change
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: The present research looks at the crucial role that Strategic Information Systems (SIS) play in promoting organizational transformation and change in the IT industry. In-depth interviews with 10 IT specialists and organizational executives are used in this research to examine important aspects, difficulties, and best practices related to SIS deployment. Important conclusions show that effective SIS deployment requires robust executive backing, thorough staff training, and strategic alignment with corporate objectives. Organizational culture also has a big influence on SIS integration, particularly collaborative vs hierarchical structures. While collaborative cultures encourage change, hierarchical structures cause resistance. Data security hazards, employee resistance, and technological complexity are often noted obstacles, and mitigating techniques including access restrictions and compliance checks have proven successful. Phased rollouts, continuous training, and constant strategic alignment are crucial, according to lessons learned from both successful and failed deployments. Organizations looking to use SIS to improve flexibility, control risks, and gain a competitive edge in the fast-paced business world of today will benefit greatly from these insights.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Wheat Stem Rust Disease Recognition Using Mask Scoring RCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Over the past 25 years, climate change has made it easier for fungal infections to spread, particularly Puccinia graminis f.sp. tritici (Pgt), which leads to wheat stem rust and offers a grave risk to global wheat output and food security. In this paper, the usage of image processing techniques and the mask-scoring R-CNN model for independent wheat stem rust recognition. With a precision of 82.92% and a Mean Intersection over Union (MIoU) of 95.32%, the model exhibits outstanding performance metrics after its training on a dataset of one thousand high-resolution photos. Using preprocessing techniques like normalization and scaling along with deep learning, the model correctly identifies wheat stem rust lesions on individual wheat leaves. Later studies combining advanced AI techniques such as meta-learning and reinforcement learning show interest in increasing the model’s adaptability to various contexts. Operating together with partners in the food system can encourage innovation, improve crop resilience, fight world hunger, and advance sustainable agricultural methods.

articleTitle: MIWO-IC Based MPPT of PV Fed Water Supply System Driven by Induction Motor with a Five Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Water supply systems through motor-pump set are required in many places including domestic, industries and agriculture. Power consume by utility grid to drive the motors is more burden and demand high reactive power due to normally using induction motors to drive water pump. Hence, powered by Photovoltaic system (PVS) based induction motor driven standalone water supply systems are providing solution for many issues including over load in grid, pollution, etc. in general, battery storage units are highly recommended for PVS based standalone power supply units. However, cost will be increased by using batteries due to regular maintenance, capital cost, replacements, safety and size etc. In fact, no need of storing power in the case of water pumping applications, instead of using batteries, the energy produced by PVS can be utilized directly to pump the water by using proper energy management and control. Hence, battery less water supply system is considered in this paper. To harvest possible maximum energy from PVS during partial shading phenomenon, the incremental conductance (IC) algorithm is combined with a MIWO: Modified invasive weed optimization technique. The IC algorithm, based on MIWO, adjusts the voltage signal reference value according to the solar irradiance on multiple panels in PVS to achieve the operation of Maximum Power Point (MPP). In order to eliminate an extra converter, a single stage system is established by working a five level inverter as a MPPT converter of the PVS. A speed sensorless control is developed on a five level inverter by balancing power between generation and consumption to manage energy management system in this paper. Hardware in the - Loop is performed on the OPAL-RT platform to test the performance of the developed model.

articleTitle: Automated Classification of Kidney Diseases Using Deep Learning: A Comparative Analysis with Machine Learning Models on CT Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: Kidney disease diagnosis with the use of a medical image plays an important role in diagnosis and treatment on time. This survey presents a comparison between different machine learning algorithms and deep learning models that classify kidney conditions from the CT KIDNEY DATASET, containing four distinct classes: Normal, Cyst, Tumor, and Stone. The authors have reviewed the performance of CNNs while comparing them against traditional machine learning models like Decision Trees, Random Forests, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, Support Vector Classifiers (SVC), Logistic Regression, K-Neighbors, Naive Bayes, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The best performance, by the CNN model, is 93.87%, which states the power of deep learning in image processing regarding medical applications. In contrast, Random Forest and Decision Tree models remain competitive within traditional classifiers with validation accuracies of 83.37% and 83.05%, respectively. Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, and SVC models come next with validation accuracies ranging from 82.73% to 79.60%, whereas KNeighbors and Naive Bayes are still farther behind, although each was performing consistently. It reflects the particular challenges associated with the application of recurrent models to static image data, best suited for temporal data. Our LSTM model realizes a test accuracy of $\mathbf{75.18 \%}$. It also points to the fact that CNNs exhibit a far better capability in detecting kidney diseases, whereas traditional models are quite viable alternatives with competitive accuracy. In fact, this essentially points out that model selection is an important issue in clinical applications, as accuracy and computational efficiency go hand in hand to enable accurate diagnosis.

articleTitle: Design of an Efficient Model for Sentiment Analysis on Twitter Using Between Fine-Tuning, Multimodal Integration, and Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: For sentiment analysis of Twitter data, a robust methodology that can effectively catch the nuances of informal language and multimodal information is essential. Previous works, though well intended, generally fail to capture the characteristics of Twitter discourse and integrate various modalities. This paper introduces a new framework for sentiment analysis using BERTweet fine-tuning, multimodal integration, and attention mechanisms for the task of sentiment analysis. BERTweet-FT would fine-tune the pre-trained BERTweet model for Twitter data, so it can capture the sentiment-related features within a tweet. Further, MM-BERTweet can leverage the textual content with additional modalities like images and user metadata, leading to rich contextual representations, which in turn provide accurate sentiment predictions. Furthermore, AGBERTweet can even add enhancements to sentiment analysis by using attention mechanisms to pick out salient words or phrases crucial for sentiment classification. Proposed Framework: Our proposed framework offers several advantages over the existing state-of-the-art baseline approaches: it improves the accuracy of sentiment classification by 5% to 12% over different ablation components. By using Twitter-specific language comprehension, multimodal information, and attention mechanisms, Our method improves Twitter data sample sentiment analysis performance. Effect of the Work: This work will have an impact on a variety of applications, where precise sentiment analysis is essential for decision-making processes, such as social media marketing strategies, public opinion analysis, and brand sentiment monitoring. By improving sentiment analysis methods specifically designed for Twitter data, this work attempts to address important issues and creates new opportunities for future study in this field.

articleTitle: Classification of Pigmented Skin Lesions using Early Fusion of Multi-Deep Features and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Sustainable Innovations in Technology (IC-SIT)
abstract: One of the primary organ is the skin. It protects and separates humans from various dangers. Nevertheless, the skin is susceptible to damage and can develop pigmented lesions. Manual classification of Pigmented Skin Lesions(PSL) is a major challenge due to availability and bias of physician, time consuming, invasive methods are painful and with elevated expenses. To overcome this, in this paper, two automated computer vision based approaches (using and without using dimensionality reduction) are employed by modelling multi-deep features using Support Vector Machine(SVM) for classification of PSL. The suggested system comprises of two operational stages. Initially, the performance of six Convolutional Neural Network models (VGG16, VGG19, AlexNet, Xception, ResNet50, and EfficientB3) in deep feature extraction and three types of hand-crafted features extraction methods (HOG, LBP, and SIFT) employing SVM are evaluated. The top three CNN models (AlexNet, ResNet50, and EfficientB3) based on accuracy are used to form binary and ternary early fusion hybrid models to classify the skin lesions. In the second stage, combining multiple CNN models resulted in increased dimensionality and number of features. These features are then classified using SVM once in the higher dimension and again by reducing the dimensionality by applying Principal Component Analysis(PCA). The accuracies of the combined models are then compared. It is observed that the ternary early fusion model with SVM (Alexnet+Resnet50+EfficientB3-SVM) produces the highest accuracy of 82.22% with higher number of features whereas the same model while using PCA produces the accuracy of 81.57%. Consequently, the findings indicate the suggested techniques are useful for classification of PSL.
